title: Getting Started with anumaan
text: anumaan R package preprocessing antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance data performing GBD-style burden estimation. takes messy hospital data produces analysis-ready, standardized datasets - handling organism antibiotic normalization, event deduplication, MDR/XDR classification, polymicrobial weighting, DALY calculations.

title: Getting Started with anumaan
text: Automated pipeline: run_preprocess() runs full sequence one call Input validation: column checks, key quality, date repair every step Organism normalization: handles typos, abbreviations, case, MRSA/CoNS flags Antibiotic classification: AWaRe categories drug classes AST cleaning: standardizes free-text R/S/values, flags invalid entries MDR/XDR classification: Magiorakos 2012 (/CDC-compliant) Event deduplication: unique infection episodes across repeat cultures Polymicrobial detection fractional weighting HAI / CAI classification: derived admission--culture date gap Diagnosis -> ICD-10 -> syndrome mapping: text, rule-based, embedding Contaminant flagging: syndrome-aware contaminant lists Attrition tracking: patient event counts every filter step DALY burden estimation: YLL, YLD, attributable associated burden Visualization: ggplot2-based resistance, burden, spatial plots

title: Getting Started with anumaan
text: run_preprocess() single entry point runs phases sequence.
code: result <- run_preprocess(   data            = sample_data,   config          = amr_config(),   phases          = "all",       # "standardize", "enrich", "derive", or "all"   verbose         = TRUE,   validate        = TRUE,   generate_report = TRUE )  clean_data     <- result$data      # preprocessed data frame config_used    <- result$config    # amr_config() object used processing_log <- result$log       # per-phase transformation logs report         <- result$report    # preprocessing report metadata       <- result$metadata  # timing, row counts, phases run

title: Compute Resistance Profile Probabilities per Pathogen — compute_resistance_profiles

QP solved via quadprog::solve.QP. small ridge term (ridge) added Hessian guarantee strict positive-definiteness. solver failure pathogen gets uniform distribution profiles.
